The reachable comparison set is proved finite and nonempty from the derived containment and seed; an actual IsGreatest true-value benchmark is constructed.
An actual monotone Finset run contained in a finite bound cannot expand strictly in all card(bound)+1 disjoint windows; equal endpoints force the entire window to remain constant.
The full run uses N = Nat horizon/(card(bound)+1), N>0, and 8*multiplier^2*information/log(1+1/lambda) <= (N:Real)*epsilon^2 exactly; it does not drop the integer floor.
A nonnegative horizon sum bounds the contained window sum; raw radius and variance hypotheses are then instantiated with the actual width-maximizing queries in that window.

The true finite maximizer is shown to be a potential maximizer, yielding f(x) <= lower(actual_report)+epsilon. Increasing lower bands and nested safe sets preserve this stronger certificate for all later actual reports.

The full theorem proves an attained optimum over the actual epsilon-reachable closure and epsilon optimality for every actual report at round >= horizon, from the explicit algorithm update and primitive confidence/variance/information hypotheses.
